title: Never Split the Difference, lesson 2 - mirror them and slow down

slides.title: Your Boss Drops A Bad Request

graphic.prompt: “Make two copies of all the paperwork.”
graphic.q: What would you say? Pick one, then swipe.

body: The book describes an office worker whose boss **loves sudden demands.**
Saying yes costs her hours. Saying no *feels risky.*

slides.title: She Said Three Words. Then Nothing.

messages.name: BOSS
messages.t: Make two copies of all the paperwork.

messages.name: BOSS
messages.t: Well, the client wants one because...

graphic.note: Then she stayed quiet, and he started explaining.

body: Instead of arguing, she calmly repeated his words **like a question.**
The boss started explaining his reasons. Now it was *a discussion*, not an order.

slides.title: This Is Called A Mirror

graphic.prompt: “I'm worried this will run over budget.”

body: Former FBI negotiator **Chris Voss** calls it _mirroring_: repeat the **last three words**, or the one to three that matter most.
Say them back gently, *like a question.* No argument, no clever comeback.

slides.title: Why It Works So Well

graphic.note: illustration: a mirror hands them the floor

body: We're drawn to people who **seem like us.** Hearing your own words back feels like being understood.
So they relax and *keep talking*, explaining what they really meant. And you get **time to think.**

slides.title: Even Waiters Get Paid For It
body: The book points to research on restaurant waiters.
Those who repeated each order back **word for word** earned *noticeably bigger tips.*

slides.title: How You Say It Matters As Much

graphic.q: Say both out loud. Hear the difference?

body: Voss recommends a **late-night FM DJ voice**: deep, slow, calm and reassuring.
Let your tone *curl downward* at the end. It signals you're in control and nobody needs to panic.

slides.title: Then Comes The Hard Part

graphic.label: say nothing
graphic.sub: count it now. it feels long.
graphic.q: Could you hold it in a tense moment?

body: After the mirror, **stay silent** for at least four seconds.
Let the mirror work. The other person *fills the silence* for you.

slides.title: Practise Before You Need It

items.they: I need this done by Friday.
We can't afford that right now.

body: Write your mirror for each line. **Just their words**, as a question.
Then imagine the *four seconds of silence* after each one.

slides.title: The Full Recipe
body: Use it in your next **tense conversation.**
Try just one mirror and *notice what they reveal.*

slides.title: One Question To Sit With

graphic.q: Who's the first person you'll mirror this week?

body: You don't need a better argument. **You need their words back.**
Save this, and follow for lesson 3. Full animated lesson at *visualgrowth.app*
